mnemonic: 결재 is sign-off on paperwork: picture the boss as a judge (재판) ruling on your report. For money it's 결제, with the 제 of 경제 (economy).

examples.ko: 팀장님 결재가 나야 비품을 주문할 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can't order supplies until the team leader signs off.

examples.ko: 보고서를 고쳐서 다시 결재를 올렸지만 아직 아무 답이 없다.
examples.en: I revised the report and resubmitted it for approval, but there's still no response.

production.promptEn: approval / sign-off (from a superior, on a document)

mnemonic: 결제 is money: it shares its 제 with 경제 (economy). Sign-off on paperwork is 결재, with the 재 of 재판 (a ruling).

examples.ko: 해외 사이트에서 결제할 때는 수수료가 붙는지 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When you pay on an overseas site, be sure to check whether a fee gets added.

examples.ko: 카드 결제가 자꾸 거절돼서 결국 계좌 이체로 보냈다.
examples.en: My card payment kept getting declined, so I ended up sending it by bank transfer.

production.promptEn: payment (settling a bill)

mnemonic: 재량껏 하세요 = 'use your own judgment.' You measure out the right amount (량, as in 분량) yourself.

collocations.en: at one's own discretion, as one sees fit

examples.ko: 회식 참석 여부는 각자 재량에 맡기겠습니다.
examples.en: Whether to come to the staff dinner is up to each of you.

examples.ko: 환불 기준이 애매할 때는 매장 직원이 재량껏 처리해도 된다.
examples.en: When the refund rules are unclear, store staff may handle it as they see fit.

production.promptEn: discretion (latitude to decide as one sees fit)

mnemonic: 버무리다 is tossing 나물 with seasoning. 얼버무리다: you toss your words together so loosely that no clear answer comes out.

collocations.en: to dodge a question, answer evasively
to speak evasively, fudge one's words

examples.ko: 언제 갚을 거냐고 묻자 그는 말끝을 흐리며 대답을 얼버무렸다.
examples.en: When asked when he'd pay it back, he trailed off and dodged the question.

examples.ko: 기자들의 질문에 대변인은 "검토 중"이라는 말로 얼버무렸다.
examples.en: The spokesperson brushed off the reporters' questions with a "we're looking into it."

examples.ko: 괜히 얼버무리지 말고 솔직하게 말해 봐.
examples.en: Stop dodging the question and just tell me honestly.

production.promptEn: to answer evasively; to gloss over (a question)

mnemonic: 결렬 has the 렬 of 분열 (split): 협상이 결렬되다, the talks tear apart.

examples.ko: 임금 협상이 끝내 결렬되면서 노조는 다음 주 파업에 들어가기로 했다.
examples.en: With wage talks finally breaking down, the union decided to strike next week.

examples.ko: 양측이 한 발씩만 물러섰어도 결렬까지는 가지 않았을 거예요.
examples.en: If each side had given just a little ground, it wouldn't have come to a breakdown.

production.promptEn: breakdown / collapse (of negotiations or talks)

mnemonic: 결단을 내리다: cut the knot (단, as in 단절 'cutting off') and decide. Don't mix it up with 결딴나다 (ruined): that's what happens when nobody decides.

examples.ko: 회사를 살리려면 대표가 결단을 내려야 할 때다.
examples.en: If the company is going to survive, it's time for the CEO to make the call.

examples.ko: 그 선배는 사람은 좋은데 결단력이 없어서 회의가 늘 길어져.
examples.en: He's a nice guy, but he can't make up his mind, so meetings always drag on.

production.promptEn: a bold decision; resolve (as in making the hard call)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; you 'hand one down' (make the call)

mnemonic: 결딴 (hard ㄸ) is a native word for ruin: 살림이 결딴나다. 결단 (soft ㄷ) is a decision. Hard ㄸ, hard landing.

examples.ko: 도박에 손을 댄 지 일 년 만에 집안 살림이 완전히 결딴났다.
examples.en: Within a year of his taking up gambling, the family's finances were completely wrecked.

examples.ko: 그 노트북 떨어뜨리면 진짜 결딴나니까 조심해.
examples.en: Careful: if you drop that laptop, it's done for.

production.promptEn: to be ruined, wrecked, done for
production.contextHint: native verb; sounds like the Sino-Korean word for 'decision'

mnemonic: 제재 = 제한 (limit) + 재판 (ruling): a ruling that puts limits on someone. 경제 제재 = economic sanctions.

examples.ko: 정부는 허위 광고를 낸 업체들에 과징금 등 제재를 가하기로 했다.
examples.en: The government decided to impose sanctions, including fines, on companies that ran false ads.

examples.ko: 규정을 어긴 선수에게 어느 정도의 제재가 적절한지를 두고 의견이 갈렸다.
examples.en: Opinions were split over how heavy a penalty was right for the player who broke the rules.

production.promptEn: sanction(s); punitive measures
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; what governments and regulators impose

mnemonic: 중재: someone standing in the middle passes judgment (재, as in 재판) between two sides. 중재에 나서다 = to step in as mediator.

collocations.en: to take on the role of mediator

examples.ko: 두 부서의 갈등이 커지자 결국 인사팀이 중재에 나섰다.
examples.en: As the conflict between the two departments grew, HR finally stepped in to mediate.

examples.ko: 형제끼리 싸울 때마다 중재하는 건 늘 막내였어요.
examples.en: Whenever the brothers fought, it was always the youngest who played peacemaker.

production.promptEn: mediation, arbitration (between two disputing sides)

mnemonic: 묵 is silence (묵묵히, 침묵); 인 is accepting (인정). 묵인 = you know, you say nothing, and you let it stand.

collocations.en: to tacitly allow, turn a blind eye to

examples.ko: 회사가 수년간 초과 근무 기록 조작을 묵인해 온 사실이 드러났다.
examples.en: It came out that the company had for years turned a blind eye to falsified overtime records.

examples.ko: 알면서도 아무 말 안 했으면 그게 묵인이지 뭐야.
examples.en: If you knew and said nothing, that's going along with it, isn't it?

production.promptEn: tacit approval; turning a blind eye (to wrongdoing)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

mnemonic: 시인하다 is 인정하다 with a wince: admitting what you'd rather not (잘못을 시인하다). Same sound as 시인 'poet'; the collocation tells you which.

examples.ko: 장관은 초기 대응이 늦었다는 점을 시인하고 공식 사과했다.
examples.en: The minister admitted that the initial response had been slow and issued a formal apology.

examples.ko: 끝까지 부인하던 그도 증거가 나오자 결국 시인할 수밖에 없었다.
examples.en: He denied it to the end, but once the evidence surfaced he had no choice but to admit it.

production.promptEn: to admit, own up to (a fault or an allegation)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean verb; formal, frequent in the news

mnemonic: 인지 shares its 인 with 인식 (awareness) and its 지 with 지식 (knowledge): the moment something registers. 인지 능력 = cognitive ability.

examples.ko: 회사 측은 문제가 발생한 지 사흘이 지나서야 이를 인지했다고 밝혔다.
examples.en: The company said it only became aware of the problem three days after it occurred.

examples.ko: 나이가 들어도 인지 능력을 유지하려면 새로운 걸 꾸준히 배우는 게 좋대요.
examples.en: They say that to keep your cognitive abilities as you age, it helps to keep learning new things.

production.promptEn: awareness, cognition (as in becoming aware of a problem)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; psychology and press-release vocabulary

mnemonic: 식견 = the 견해 (views) of someone with 지식 (knowledge): you see because you know what you're looking at. 짧은 식견 is a humble formula.

examples.ko: 그분은 미술사에 대한 식견이 깊어서 전시 기획을 맡기기에 딱이다.
examples.en: Her deep insight into art history makes her the ideal person to curate the exhibition.

examples.ko: 제 짧은 식견으로는 이 계획이 다소 성급해 보입니다.
examples.en: In my limited view, this plan looks a bit hasty.

production.promptEn: insight, discernment (judgment informed by knowledge)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; 'my short ~' is a humble formula

mnemonic: 면 is face (면접, 대면); 식 is knowing (지식). 일면식도 없다 = 'never so much as seen their face.'

collocations.en: to have never met at all
a perpetrator known to the victim

examples.ko: 일면식도 없는 사람한테서 갑자기 동업 제안이 왔다.
examples.en: Out of the blue I got a partnership offer from someone I'd never even met.

examples.ko: 현관문이 부서지지 않은 점으로 미루어 경찰은 면식범의 소행일 가능성에 무게를 두고 있다.
examples.en: Since the front door wasn't forced, police are leaning toward the theory that the culprit knew the victim.

production.promptEn: acquaintance (having met someone; knowing them by face)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; usually in 'never even met'

mnemonic: 식별 = knowing (지식) + telling apart (구별). 식별이 어렵다 = hard to tell apart.

collocations.en: to be hard to make out

examples.ko: 화질이 너무 낮아서 차량 번호판을 식별할 수 없었다.
examples.en: The image quality was too poor to make out the license plate.

examples.ko: 안개가 너무 짙어서 바로 앞차도 식별이 안 될 정도였어요.
examples.en: The fog was so thick you could barely make out the car right in front of you.

production.promptEn: identification; telling apart / making out (visually)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

mnemonic: 논란 = an argument (논쟁) that's hard (난, as in 곤란) to settle. 논란이 일다 = a controversy flares up.

examples.ko: 시청이 공원 부지에 주차장을 짓겠다고 발표하자 논란이 일었다.
examples.en: Controversy erupted when City Hall announced it would build a parking lot on the park site.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 과거 발언 때문에 또다시 논란에 휩싸였다.
examples.en: The actor is embroiled in controversy yet again over past remarks.

examples.ko: 그건 논란의 여지가 없는 사실이야.
examples.en: That's an indisputable fact.

production.promptEn: controversy (a public dispute)

mnemonic: 반론 = 반대 + 논리: an argument pushed back the other way. 반론의 여지 = room for objection.

examples.ko: 발표가 끝나자 한 교수가 표본이 너무 작다며 반론을 제기했다.
examples.en: When the presentation ended, a professor objected that the sample was too small.

examples.ko: 네 말에 반론하려는 건 아닌데, 다른 가능성도 있지 않을까?
examples.en: I'm not trying to argue with you, but couldn't there be another explanation?

production.promptEn: counterargument, rebuttal

mnemonic: 논조 = 논리 + 어조 (tone): the key an argument is played in. 비판적인 논조 = a critical tone.

examples.ko: 같은 사건인데도 신문마다 논조가 확연히 달랐다.
examples.en: It was the same incident, yet each paper's slant was strikingly different.

examples.ko: 선거가 가까워지자 그 매체의 논조가 눈에 띄게 누그러졌다.
examples.en: As the election drew near, the outlet's tone noticeably softened.

production.promptEn: the tone or slant of an argument (e.g., of an editorial)

mnemonic: 개입 = stepping in (입, as in 입장 'entry') as a go-between (개, as in 소개). 외부 개입 = outside interference.

examples.ko: 중앙은행이 환율 방어를 위해 시장에 개입했다.
examples.en: The central bank intervened in the market to defend the exchange rate.

examples.ko: 남의 부부 싸움에는 괜히 개입하지 않는 게 좋아.
examples.en: Better not to get involved in other couples' fights.

production.promptEn: intervention; getting involved (in another party's affairs)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

mnemonic: 개의 is what gets between you and your peace of mind (개 as in 소개, 의 as in 의식). 개의치 않다 = it doesn't get to you. Almost always negated.

collocations.en: to not care what others think
to not mind in the slightest
please don't give it a thought

examples.ko: 그는 남들이 뭐라고 하든 개의치 않고 자기 방식대로 밀고 나갔다.
examples.en: Whatever others said, he paid no heed and pushed ahead his own way.

examples.ko: 답장이 늦어 죄송합니다. — 아닙니다, 개의치 마세요.
examples.en: Sorry for the late reply. — Not at all, please don't give it a thought.

production.promptEn: to not mind; to pay no heed (to)

mnemonic: 경위 uses the 경 of 경도 (longitude) and the 위 of 위도 (latitude): the warp and weft, the whole weave of how it happened. 사건의 경위 = how the incident came about. 경위서 is an incident report.

examples.ko: 경찰은 화재가 발생한 경위를 조사하고 있다.
examples.en: Police are investigating how the fire started.

examples.ko: 지각한 경위를 경위서로 써서 내라고 하더라.
examples.en: They told me to submit a written report explaining how I came to be late.

production.promptEn: the circumstances; how something came about (of an incident)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun; add a suffix for 'incident report'

mnemonic: 신경 (nerves) + 전 (war, as in 전쟁): exactly what it says.

collocations.en: to wage a war of nerves

examples.ko: 회의 내내 두 팀장은 예산을 두고 보이지 않는 신경전을 벌였다.
examples.en: Throughout the meeting the two team leads waged an unspoken war of nerves over the budget.

examples.ko: 누가 먼저 연락하나 신경전을 벌이다가 결국 한 달 동안 말도 안 했어.
examples.en: We were in a standoff over who'd reach out first and ended up not speaking for a month.

production.promptEn: a war of nerves; tense standoff

mnemonic: 구제 shares its 구 with 구조 (rescue): help for people who can't get out alone. 구제 금융 = a bailout.

examples.ko: 정부는 전세 사기 피해자 구제를 위한 특별법을 추진하고 있다.
examples.en: The government is pushing a special law to provide relief to victims of rental deposit fraud.

examples.ko: 외환 위기 때 우리나라는 국제통화기금의 구제 금융을 받았다.
examples.en: During the currency crisis, Korea took a bailout from the IMF.

examples.ko: 방 꼴 좀 봐라. 넌 진짜 구제 불능이다.
examples.en: Look at the state of this room. You're truly hopeless.

production.promptEn: relief / rescue (for victims or the distressed)

mnemonic: 미 means 'not yet' (미정 'undecided', 미완성 'unfinished'): a case not yet closed. (미제 alone can also mean 'American-made'; context decides.)

examples.ko: 장기 미제 사건으로 남아 있던 이십 년 전 강도 살인의 범인이 DNA 재감정으로 붙잡혔다.
examples.en: Renewed DNA testing led to the arrest of the culprit in a twenty-year-old robbery-murder that had remained a cold case.

examples.ko: 그 실종 사건은 끝내 미제로 남았다.
examples.en: That disappearance was never solved.

production.promptEn: an unsolved (criminal) case; a cold case
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun phrase; police and news

mnemonic: 구축 = 구조 (structure) + 건축 (building): building systems, networks, and trust rather than houses.

examples.ko: 두 기관은 정보 공유를 위한 협력 체계를 구축하기로 합의했다.
examples.en: The two agencies agreed to set up a framework for sharing information.

examples.ko: 새 팀장은 부임하자마자 팀원들과 신뢰 관계를 구축하는 데 공을 들였다.
examples.en: From day one, the new manager put real effort into building trust with her team.

production.promptEn: building / establishing (a system, network, or relationship)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

mnemonic: 허 is empty (허무, 허공): a structure (구조) with nothing inside. It looks solid, but it's made up.

collocations.en: to turn out to be fabricated

examples.ko: 이 소설은 실화를 바탕으로 했지만 인물 대부분은 허구다.
examples.en: The novel is based on a true story, but most of the characters are fictional.

examples.ko: 그가 내세운 화려한 경력은 상당 부분 허구로 드러났다.
examples.en: Much of the glittering résumé he touted turned out to be made up.

production.promptEn: fiction; fabrication (something made up)

mnemonic: 환산 = 환전 (exchanging money) + 계산 (calculating): doing the math to swap one unit for another. 원화로 환산하면 = converted into won.

collocations.en: to work out as an hourly wage

examples.ko: 연봉을 시급으로 환산해 보니 최저 임금에도 못 미쳤다.
examples.en: When I worked my salary out as an hourly wage, it didn't even reach minimum wage.

examples.ko: 해외 매출은 모두 원화로 환산해서 보고서에 기재해 주세요.
examples.en: Please convert all overseas sales into won before entering them in the report.

production.promptEn: conversion (of currency or units)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb

mnemonic: 치환 = 배치 (putting in place) + 교환 (swapping): put one thing in another's place.

examples.ko: 수식에서 x를 다른 변수로 치환하면 훨씬 간단해진다.
examples.en: If you substitute another variable for x, the equation gets much simpler.

examples.ko: 그 감독의 영화는 사회 문제를 개인의 감정 문제로 치환해 버린다는 비판을 받는다.
examples.en: That director's films are criticized for recasting social problems as matters of personal feeling.

production.promptEn: substitution (replacing one element with another, in math, code, or analysis)

mnemonic: 지양 has the 지 of 중지 (stop): what you steer clear of. Its look-alike 지향 has the 향 of 방향 (direction): where you're heading. Not 지향 (aim for).

collocations.en: an attitude to steer clear of

examples.ko: 학교는 성적만으로 학생을 평가하는 방식을 지양하겠다고 밝혔다.
examples.en: The school said it would move away from judging students on grades alone.

examples.ko: 회의에서 특정인을 겨냥한 비난은 지양해 주시기 바랍니다.
examples.en: Please refrain from criticism aimed at specific individuals during the meeting.

production.promptEn: avoiding / steering clear of (something undesirable)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'aim for'

mnemonic: 지향 has the 향 of 방향 (direction): where you're heading (미래 지향적). Its look-alike 지양 has the 지 of 중지 (stop): what you steer clear of. Not 지양 (avoid).

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 단기 수익보다 지속 가능한 성장을 지향한다.
examples.en: Our company aims for sustainable growth over short-term profit.

examples.ko: 그 정당은 중도를 지향한다고 하지만 실제 정책은 꽤 다르다.
examples.en: The party says it aims for the center, but its actual policies are quite different.

production.promptEn: aiming for; orientation toward (a goal or direction)
production.contextHint: Sino-Korean noun, often as a verb; NOT the near-homophone meaning 'avoid'

examples.ko: 야심 차게 준비한 기획안이었는데 임원들 반응이 영 시큰둥했다.
examples.en: I'd poured a lot into that proposal, but the executives' reaction was distinctly lukewarm.

examples.ko: 선물을 줬더니 "응, 고마워" 하고 시큰둥하게 말하더라.
examples.en: I gave her the present and she just went "Yeah, thanks" with zero enthusiasm.

production.promptEn: unenthusiastic, lukewarm (of a reaction)

mnemonic: 넌지시 slides in sideways, like a question asked while looking at something else.

collocations.en: to ask in a roundabout way

examples.ko: 엄마는 결혼 계획이 있냐고 넌지시 물어보셨다.
examples.en: Mom asked, in a roundabout way, whether I had any plans to get married.

examples.ko: 선배가 이번 인사에서 우리 팀에 변화가 있을 거라고 넌지시 귀띔해 줬다.
examples.en: A senior colleague quietly tipped me off that our team would see changes in this round of personnel moves.

production.promptEn: subtly, by way of a hint (asking or suggesting indirectly)

mnemonic: 어영부영 drifts like its own sound: no shape, no plan, and suddenly the day is gone.

examples.ko: 주말 내내 어영부영하다 보니 벌써 일요일 밤이네.
examples.en: I frittered the whole weekend away and now it's already Sunday night.

examples.ko: 어영부영 시간만 보내다가는 졸업할 때 후회할 거야.
examples.en: If you just drift along, you'll regret it when you graduate.

production.promptEn: idly, aimlessly (letting time slip by without doing anything properly)

mnemonic: 걷잡다 = gather in and grab hold (걷다 as in 빨래를 걷다). 겉잡다, with ㅌ, means 'estimate by the surface': a different word.

collocations.en: a situation spiraling out of control

examples.ko: 강풍을 타고 불길이 걷잡을 수 없이 번졌다.
examples.en: Fanned by strong winds, the flames spread out of control.

examples.ko: 처음에 바로 해명했어야지. 이제는 소문이 걷잡을 수 없게 됐잖아.
examples.en: You should have explained right away. Now the rumor has gotten completely out of hand.

production.promptEn: uncontrollable; (spreading) out of control
production.contextHint: native; built on a verb that's always negated ('cannot ~')

mnemonic: 띠 is a sash: you 띠다 a quality the way you wear a sash (미소를 띠다, 활기를 띠다). 눈에 띄다 is the other word.
meanings: to take on (a color, mood, quality)

collocations.en: to be charged with a mission

examples.ko: 연말이 다가오자 상가 거리가 모처럼 활기를 띠었다.
examples.en: With the year's end approaching, the shopping street came alive for once.

examples.ko: 그는 입가에 옅은 미소를 띤 채 질문을 끝까지 들었다.
examples.en: With a faint smile on his lips, he listened to the question to the end.

production.promptEn: to take on / be tinged with (a color, mood, or quality); to wear (a smile)
production.contextHint: native verb; NOT the near-homophone 'to catch the eye'

mnemonic: 곱 double (as in 곱절) + 씹다 chew: chewing it twice, like a cow with its cud.

collocations.en: to turn someone's words over in one's mind

examples.ko: 면접관이 마지막에 한 말을 집에 오는 내내 곱씹었다.
examples.en: All the way home I kept turning over what the interviewer said at the end.

examples.ko: 지난 일을 자꾸 곱씹어 봤자 너만 힘들어.
examples.en: Going over the past again and again only wears you down.

production.promptEn: to mull over / dwell on (words or events) again and again

examples.ko: 반갑게 손을 흔들었는데 다른 사람이어서 머쓱하게 손을 내렸다.
examples.en: I waved happily, but it was someone else, so I sheepishly lowered my hand.

examples.ko: 아무도 내 농담에 안 웃어서 괜히 머쓱해졌어.
examples.en: Nobody laughed at my joke, and I felt kind of silly.

production.promptEn: sheepish, awkward (after being rebuffed or ignored)

meanings: to drag in (a name, the past)

examples.ko: 그는 걸핏하면 회장 이름을 들먹이며 자기 뜻을 밀어붙였다.
examples.en: At every turn he'd invoke the chairman's name to get his way.

examples.ko: 다 지난 일을 왜 자꾸 들먹여?
examples.en: Why do you keep dragging up things that are over and done with?

production.promptEn: to keep bringing up / drag in (a name or the past), usually for leverage

mnemonic: 꾸역꾸역: the sound of cramming in one more bite, one more task, one more step.

collocations.en: to drag oneself to work anyway

examples.ko: 입맛이 하나도 없었지만 약을 먹어야 해서 밥을 꾸역꾸역 밀어 넣었다.
examples.en: I had no appetite, but I had to take my medicine, so I forced the rice down.

examples.ko: 하기 싫어도 꾸역꾸역 하다 보면 어느새 끝나 있더라.
examples.en: Even when you don't feel like it, if you just grind away, it's done before you know it.

production.promptEn: doggedly, forcing oneself on (despite reluctance); stuffing food in

mnemonic: 자못 is 꽤 in a suit and tie: you'll meet it in reviews and essays, not in chat.

examples.ko: 신인 감독의 첫 작품치고는 완성도가 자못 높다.
examples.en: For a debut film, its polish is considerable.

examples.ko: 결과 발표를 앞두고 회의실에는 자못 긴장된 분위기가 감돌았다.
examples.en: Ahead of the announcement, a rather tense mood hung over the conference room.

production.promptEn: quite, considerably (written, slightly literary)
